title.narrative: Support to Peace Initiatives in CDTY

description.narrative: South Sudan is in a turbulent political situation marred by fratricidal hatred, war, tribal clashes, ethnic cleansing, more tension is building up leading to killings, and the end might be worst culminating in total extinction of some tribes like the case of Rwanda in 1994. Political insecurity is mushrooming in the Country; the reason attributed to this is breakdown of law, disintegration of social fabrics and loss of common values, persistent failures in system of governance and immature democracy. The state of affairs is becoming increasingly alarming in Western Equatoria State. Violence is spreading across the whole state, people have become suspicious of each other, and mistrust is on the increase, tribes are living in fear and contempt of one another, language is shifting from friendly to bitter exchange of words signifying a war of words. Every indicator exists to tell that, all is not right. Informal groupings are beginning to emerge entertaining different ideologies. We are witnesses to this especially in the counties of Mvolo, Mundri, Maridi, Yambio and Tombura. This situation is potentially dangerous for peaceful coexistence and nation building. It requires collective efforts and goes beyond tribal, ethnic, regional and religious lines. It equally calls upon concerted efforts especially in pooling resources together to support Peace efforts. The Diocese has been at the forefront in spearheading peace brokering, negotiations and reconciling disgruntled parties. We have brokered peace between nomadic pastoralists and Farmers conflicting over grazing and farming land. The Diocese has intervened in peace negotiations in joint forum with Inter Church Committee in their efforts in promoting dialogue with the Lord’s Resistance Army of Joseph Kony. The Diocese has organized several peace conferences, peace sports, Youths for peace and Inter-Border Peace Congress with neighbouring countries like Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. Following the recent upheavals in Western Equatoria State particularly in Mvolo, Mundri, Maridi, Yambio and Tombura; Our Church has played significant role in initiating peace talks and dialogue. The crisis in Western Equatoria has created humanitarian crisis with results reaching too far as many deaths, thousands displaced, orphaned, widowed, leaving some amputated. The worst hit categories being women and children. The Church could not fall silent but speak out on behalf and in defense of the defenceless/voiceless. Several successful discussions have been launched led by the Bishop of CDTY with peace as the ultimate objective. CDTY is calling for support from other partners like CTP to help strengthen the capacity of the diocese with financial support to facilitate their planned meetings with government officials, Elders, chiefs, church leaders and Inter-Church Committees for peace.
